newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russian tanker oil slick threatens Japan coast.
newsitem.headline: Russian tanker oil slick threatens Japan coast.

text.p: An oil slick threatened Japan's western coastline on Friday after a Russian-registered oil tanker sprang a leak, a Maritime Safety Agency spokesman said.
A large volume of heavy oil had gushed from the listing tanker, abandoned by the crew members 150 km (90 miles) northeast of the Oki Islands in the Sea of Japan, the spokesman said.
"Our helicopter sent to the area witnessed an oil slick leaking from the forward, prow end of the tanker... a belt of oil 1,000 feet (300 metres) by 1.1 miles (1.8 km)," the spokesman said.

About two-thirds of the 19,000 tonnes of the C grade oil on board the 13,157-tonne Nakhodka had already leaked out and there were fears of environmental damage to Japan's western coastline, the spokesman said.

"The slick is headed right for the Japanese coast and will likely hit the central region from as far south as Kyoto and Fukui prefecture and as far north as Ishikawa prefecture in the Noto peninsula," the spokesman said.
"The coastline under threat is noted for its beauty... we also fear there will be a large effect on the fishing industry in the area, which is a significant part of the local economy."
The spokesman could not predict when the slick would likely hit the coast, adding that much depended on the weather.

Waves of more than 20 feet (six metres) prevented the agency from halting the leak and containing the spread of the slick, which was being driven towards the Japanese coast by the prevailing wind, the spokesman said.
The spokesman said interviews with crew members indicated the tanker, which was constructed in 1970, may have ruptured under the force of heavy waves while enroute from China to Russia.
A Russian emergencies ministry spokesman said on Thursday that the vessel had broken into two.
Japanese authorities found 31 of the tanker's 32 crew adrift in life boats in rough seas on Thursday but were still searching for the captain.
"Captain Valery Melnikov was the only one among the 32 crew members who was not rescued... The chances of his survival are very slim," the Maritime Agency spokesman said.
